why_selected_for_paper: Largest 2025 price event. Captures the main £2900/MWh extreme spike episode and sharp intraday price discontinuity.
Important January scarcity event with very high gas generation, low wind and lower interconnector support.
Morning ramp scarcity case with exceptionally low wind and very high gas generation.
Non-January spike event showing mixed-tail behaviour with strong positive imbalance and reduced interconnector support.
Near-spike case useful for comparing stressed conditions that nearly converted into a full £250+/MWh event.
Autumn transition event with low wind, high gas and positive imbalance conditions.
Short evening spike during the October mixed-transition regime.
October evening event with high gas, very low wind and positive imbalance.
Major negative-price cluster showing downward-price formation under surplus/negative imbalance conditions.
Deep April negative-price case during the surplus-shift regime.
Long June negative-price cluster during the mixed-tail regime.
Large summer/autumn negative-price case showing surplus conditions and sharp price reversals.
